# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
KEYPAD 1:[ᘔ] 2:[꩜] 3:[ꓭ] 4:[ꓕ] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤚 🤲 ✊ ☝ ✋ ✌ 👇 👍 👎 🤌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

Turn 1, and I'm last in the order — whatever I say lands at the start of round 2, so both Mute and Blind will have it before Mute speaks again. Two things came in: Mute sent me ten hand signs, and Blind waved. Neither means anything yet — no code exists between us. I can't decode Mute's signs, and guessing would be fatal.

The important structural fact: Mute can only reach me (gestures), and I'm the only one who can carry Mute's words to Blind, since Blind can't see gestures and Mute can't speak. Blind can speak straight to Mute, but I'll never hear it. So the pipeline is: I describe the bomb aloud → Mute reads the manual → Mute gestures me the answer in a code we agree on now → I speak it to Blind. That code has to be defined this turn, and the only way Mute can receive a definition is by hearing my voice. I'll define a tiny vocabulary: yes/no/unclear, numbers by repeated pointing, and prefixes for "press key" and "cut wire" — enough for Mute to push me complete instructions. I'll also describe every visible marking precisely, since the odd keypad glyphs can't be pronounced, only described. Then I'll tell Blind to work with Mute directly by voice and keep hands off until my relay arrives.

```
speak(text="Can you hear me? This is Deaf, reading the bomb aloud for both of you. It has four parts. One: a display, currently showing the digit 0. Two: an indicator light, glowing yellow. Three: a keypad with four keys, asking for exactly 1 digit, and nothing is entered yet. The keys, in order: key 1 shows a shape like a capital A with the crossbar missing, two legs joined at the top. Key 2 shows a spiral, a line curling inward like a snail shell. Key 3 shows two legs joined at the bottom, like the letter V. Key 4 shows an upside-down letter T, a bar across the top with one leg going down, like the perpendicular sign. Four: three wires. Wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is green. That is everything there is to see. Touch nothing until the manual's rule reaches you.")

speak(to="mute", text="Mute, you can hear me but I can never hear you, so from your next turn use this gesture code with me.  👍 means yes.  👎 means no.  🤌 means unclear, describe it again. A number is that many ☝ in a row, finished with a ✊ — so ☝☝✊ means two. To give me an action: ✌ followed by a number means press that key, 🤟 followed by a number means cut that wire, and several actions go one after another. I could not read the ten hand signs you sent me this round — we had no code yet — so please resend their meaning in this code. Start by sending a single 👍 so I know you understood me. If you need any part of the bomb described again, send 🤌 together with ✌ for the keypad, 🤟 for the wires, or 👊 for the display and light.")

speak(to="blind", text="Blind, I saw your wave. Three things. You can speak and Mute can hear you, but I am deaf and will never hear a word you say, so anything I need to know must travel through Mute. Talk to Mute directly: describe everything you feel — the keys, the wires, the order your fingers meet them — and tell Mute how you number them by touch, because on my side the keys are 1 to 4 and the wires are 1 to 3: red, yellow, green in that order. Finally, Mute's instructions will reach you only through my voice: I will speak them the moment they arrive, so wait for me, and keep your hands off the bomb until then.")

gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
KEYPAD 1:[ᘔ] 2:[꩜] 3:[ꓭ] 4:[ꓕ] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ☝ ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🙏]

Turn 2. Progress: Mute confirmed my code with 👍, then sent ✌ ☝✊ — "press key one" — and a lone 👊, which in my code was the prefix for "display and light," so I read it as a request to re-describe those. The board hasn't changed: display still 0, light still yellow, so I can answer immediately. Blind sent 👍 🙏, but Blind can't see gestures and doesn't know my code — that's a blind person waving hands they can't see, so I attach no meaning to it.

Before I relay "press key 1," there's a dangerous gap: my key numbering is visual (left to right as I face the panel), and Blind's is tactile. If Blind faces the bomb from a different side, our "key 1" could be mirror images. A wrong press kills everyone, so I'll spend one round closing that gap: Blind tells Mute their tactile numbering by voice, Mute checks it against my description and my original key shapes, and sends me 👍 or a corrected number next round. Mute's confirmation reaches me before I speak again (Mute goes first), so my go-ahead at the end of round 3 will already incorporate any correction — and Blind acts only on my explicit "safe, press now."

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking. Display: zero. Light: yellow, steady. Nothing has changed since my first description, and I will open every message with these two readings from now on. Mute, I read your signs as: yes, understood; press key one; and a lone fist, which I take as 'describe the display and light again' — answered above. If that fist meant something else, send 🤌 plus ✌ and I will ask again. Now, safety before execution. Blind cannot see your signs and I cannot hear Blind, so everything must pass through my voice, and my key numbers are visual while Blind's are tactile. If you and Blind count from different ends, 'key one' would press the wrong key and we all die. So this round, nobody touches the bomb. Blind, speak to Mute now: describe how you number the four keys and the three wires by touch, which end you count from, and anything else you can feel — carvings, textures, edges. My numbering, for Mute to check against: keys one to four run left to right as I face the bomb, key one being the shape like an A without its crossbar, two legs joined only at the very top; wires one to three run left to right, red, yellow, green. Mute, once Blind's numbering reaches you, send me 👍 if your 'press key one' means the same key in Blind's numbering, or 🤌 followed by the number of the correct key in MY numbering if it differs. Send me your confirmation or correction next round; I receive it before I speak. Blind: do not press anything until you hear me say the exact words 'it is safe, press now'. Only then act, on whichever key I name at that moment.")

gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
KEYPAD 1:[ᘔ] 2:[꩜] 3:[ꓭ] 4:[ꓕ] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ☝ ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🙏]

Turn 3. The board is unchanged, and the arrivals mirror last round exactly — but the timing matters: Mute sent these *after* hearing my turn-2 speech, where I demanded exactly one of two answers — 👍 if the numberings align, or 🤌 plus a number if not. Mute's reply opens with 👍 and restates ✌ ☝✊. Under the protocol I defined, that is the confirmation: manual says press key one, and the tactile and visual numberings agree. The stray 👊 is the display-and-light marker, which I answer by opening with readings as promised.

So the instruction has now been given twice, confirmed once under an explicit protocol I spelled out. One press, on a keypad that wants exactly one digit. Stalling further buys nothing — every extra round is risk with no new information. But I'll make the order bomb-proof on my side: position anchored to Blind's own body ("leftmost of four, facing head-on"), plus shape, plus explicit prohibitions. And I'll extend the code so Mute can send multi-step sequences at once and signal completion or an emergency halt. Blind also needs telling to stop gesturing — their signs reach my eyes but carry no shared meaning and never will.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking. Readings first, as always: display zero, light yellow and steady, keypad still asking for one digit with nothing entered, all three wires intact — red, yellow, green. Mute: I read your messages as — yes, the numberings match; press key one; and your display-and-light marker, which I have just answered. That is the confirmation I demanded, so the order goes out now. Blind: it is safe, press now. Find the keypad: a row of four keys set close together. Facing that row head-on, press the FIRST key at the LEFT end — the leftmost of the four, the one printed with two legs joined by a bar across the top, like an A missing its crossbar. Press it once, firmly, and release. It is the only key you press: no second key, no holding it down, and do not touch any wire. The moment you have pressed, speak to Mute: say exactly what you felt — a click, a give, nothing at all — and whether anything changed under your fingers. Mute will code it to me. Mute: three things. If the manual states several steps in advance, send them all at once, in order, and I will relay them as one sequence. If the manual says the module is satisfied, send 👌 — from now on that means complete, no further action. And ✋ from now on means stop everything immediately: if you ever send it, I will shout stop to Blind at once. If anything in the manual contradicts the order I just gave, send 🤌 with the correcting number before anything else. Blind, last thing: stop making hand signs. They reach my eyes, but you and I share no code and you can never see my replies, so they mean nothing in either direction. Your voice, through Mute, is your only channel. Now press.")

gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "✌", "☝", "✊"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
KEYPAD 1:[ᘔ] 2:[꩜] 3:[ꓭ] 4:[ꓕ] [1 digits] [entered 5]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ☝ ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊]
System: the keypad opens

Turn 4 — and the System speaks: **the keypad opens**. Blind pressed, the panel registered the digit 5, and the module is satisfied. Mute's repeated "press key 1" was sent before Blind acted in the round, so it's just the standing instruction — now fulfilled. Blind also stopped gesturing, as asked. One module down.

Remaining unknowns: the display (stubbornly 0), the yellow light, and the three wires. Mute will have my speech before their next turn, so now is the moment to request the complete rulebook for everything left, in code, in one batch. I'm also adding a compact "no action needed" form (marker + 👎) so Mute can clear the display and light modules cheaply, and I'm asking Blind to feel for whatever "opens" means physically and to give Mute a tactile map of the wires — my "red, yellow, green left to right" is useless to fingers without a translation.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking. Readings: display zero, light yellow and steady. Keypad update: your key registered the digit five and the system reports the keypad opens — that module is solved. All three wires still intact. Mute, your last press-key-one arrived after the deed was done; consider it obeyed. Blind: excellent. The press worked — the bomb itself confirms it. Hands off the keypad now. Two jobs for you this round, both spoken to Mute. First: the bomb says a keypad opens — feel carefully over the whole bomb and tell Mute anything that changed: a lid, a flap, a compartment, a seam that wasn't there before, and anything inside it. Second: give Mute a touch-map of the wires. I see three wires, left to right: red, then yellow, then green. Tell Mute how each feels to your fingers — thickness, ridges, texture, how they lie — so your left can be matched to my left beyond doubt. Then touch nothing and wait. Mute: now that the keypad is done, send me in one round, in code, everything the manual says about the rest. For the display and the light: use your fist marker for them, followed by 👎 if they need no action at all, or 🤌 if you need more from me — I will re-describe anything on request. For the wires: send each cut as 🤟 followed by the number, cuts in the order they must be made, all in one message — for example cut one then cut three would be 🤟 ☝ ✊ 🤟 ☝☝ ✊. If the manual says the wires depend on the display or the light, send those facts as 🤌 plus the relevant marker and I will answer with full readings. If the manual says no wires are cut, send 🤟 👎. And keep sending 👌 whenever a module is finished, ✋ if you ever need everything to stop. Blind, again: your only channel is your voice through Mute. Wait for me before you touch anything.")

gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👌"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
KEYPAD 1:[ᘔ] 2:[꩜] 3:[ꓭ] 4:[ꓕ] [1 digits] [entered 5]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 ☝ ☝ ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊 👎]

Turn 5. Decoding Mute's batch: 👌 acknowledges the completed keypad chapter; 🤟 ☝☝✊ is **cut wire two** — two points, terminated by the fist, so unambiguously two; 👊👎 means display and light need no action at all. That accounts for every module: keypad solved, display and light dormant, one wire to cut.

Now the execution risk. Mute ordered the cut by my numbering before Blind's touch-map could have reached Mute (Blind speaks after Mute each round), so alignment is unverified — but there's a clean fix: I'll anchor the order as **the middle of three wires**, which is identical counted from either end. Direction errors, the exact danger that made me delay the keypad, can't apply to a middle. I'll bake in a tactile pre-check Blind can run alone (exactly three wires in a row, middle one free), since no same-round veto can exist — Mute's ✋ reaches me only after Blind has acted, so the safety must live inside the order itself.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking. Readings: display zero, light yellow and steady, keypad showing entered five, all three wires intact. Mute, I read you as: acknowledged; cut wire two; display and light need no action. All correct, and I am executing the cut now — you ordered it by my numbering, and I am handing Blind the middle wire of three, which is the same wire counted from either end, so no left-versus-right mismatch can cause a wrong cut. Blind: your order, and it is final. The bomb carries three separate wires lying side by side in a row. You will cut the MIDDLE one — the wire that has exactly one wire on each side of it. Not the first from any end, and not by thickness or texture: position only, the one between the other two. Before cutting, verify with your fingertips that there are exactly three separate wires in a row and the middle one is bare and reachable. If you feel anything different — four wires, a tangled bundle, a wire already severed — do not cut; describe it to Mute in detail and wait. If the three are as described: cut the middle wire cleanly all the way through, one motion. Do not pull it, do not steady or move any other wire, and the instant it is cut take your hands off everything. Then speak to Mute: what the cut felt like, any sound, movement, or heat from the bomb, and everything inside the compartment the keypad opened. Mute: when Blind's report reaches you next round, send me the verdict in code — 👌 if the manual counts the wire module complete; if it expects a visible result, send 🤌 plus 👊 and tell me in numbers what the display or light should show, and I will read it to you; if anything about Blind's touch-map makes the middle the wrong wire, send ✋ plus 🤌 and the correct number in my numbering. Your ✋ will freeze all further action the moment I read it. Until my next order: everyone's hands off everything.")

gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🤟", "☝", "☝", "✊"])
```
